reviews.reason: Gather transfers already exposed source stock; it does not establish that a fallen branch has separable bark or extract that bark. Probe can support inspection but does not implement conserved bark removal. Develop a minimal inspect-and-strip method. The observed branch sources and owned stone are candidates, not verified bark supplies; no successful yield can be promised from the supplied facts.
reviews.experienceReview: Successful inspection or stripping may provide satisfying confirmed understanding when it establishes genuinely new observed information, not merely a new label or completed study. Subscribe qualified information-confirmed from inspect-strip-bark to the existing grounded-understanding source, not a duplicate source: participant is the performing observer; require recorded physical evidence and a newly confirmed finding. Reuse its 0.8 transient amount, cap 1, eight-round duration, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown; sustained gain 0.035 per qualifying event, bounded by the same source cap, with decay 0.0015 per round. Repeated known findings and routine bark output confer no additional discovery reward. No separate pleasure or mastery reward is justified by the supplied experience; nutrition, health and protected mental accounts remain unchanged.
reviews.visualReview: Inspection displays the actual target outline and an evidence panel distinguishing verified layer, unsuitable material and unresolved composition. Stripping shows the retained stone, stage progress, removed layer or fragments, and the substrate's actual changed condition; only completed, conserved outputs appear in inventory or on the ground. Replay binds these changes to the declared events and resolved material identities. Do not display successful peeling, bark stacks or apparatus before those physical effects occur.
reviews.specification: Implement versioned inspect-strip-bark, reusing probe observation and shared material-transfer code without claiming functional equivalence. Public schema: {mode:'inspect'|'strip',target:string,tool:string}; all fields required, additionalProperties:false; tool may be empty for inspection. Shared references: target resolves one visible source object or owned material item; tool resolves one owned item. Freeze resolved identities during work. Require individual learning, live actor, and actual interaction reach 0.65 using shared obstacle geometry; inspection cannot reach through solids. State: per-substrate measured outer-layer identity, remaining layer mass, separability, intact-sheet area, moisture, inspection evidence and extraction history; unknown fields remain unknown. Inspection costs one round and 0.2 energy, examining actual supported material state; report verified suitability, unsuitable, or unresolved, never infer bark from resource name. A positive result requires an actual separable bark layer whose properties meet food-assay's bark-sheet requirements. Stripping requires that verified layer and an owned stone with hardness at least 8. Reserve at most 0.12 mass of that finite layer, not additional source stock; perform two work rounds costing 0.5 energy each. At each paid stage remove the corresponding reserved mass from the substrate, retain it as partially processed material, and update substrate mass and condition. Completion returns the actual recovered mass as bark only if it meets the measured requirements; bark quantity equals recovered mass/0.3, with no rounding-created material. Failed separation retains real fragments, not assay-grade sheets. Never grant bark in addition to unchanged branch mass; preserve substrate identity, source provenance, remaining wood, fragments and losses in a conserved ledger. Source gathering and extraction share locks and composition accounting so neither can duplicate material. No felling, source regeneration, or assay construction is included. Missing energy or temporarily inaccessible tool pauses without charges; global pauses preserve exact work. Action change, movement out of reach, substrate destruction or death cancels once: release surviving unremoved reservations to their original substrate and return removed material to its owner, or drop it at the work location if dead; never refund spent energy or restore removed layers. Store actual remaining work; cancelled partial material remains physical but cannot be completed for free. Declare bark-inspected, bark-strip-progress, bark-stripped and bark-strip-stopped, plus qualified information-confirmed events. Bind paid stages, evidence, material quantities and uncertainty to event records and replay. Migration adds nullable material-layer fields and conservation bookkeeping, not bark stock or positive suitability. Existing generic branch sources remain unresolved unless their actual material representation supports verification; otherwise inspection explicitly reports the missing physical evidence. Dependencies are actual layer-bearing material, retained stone for stripping, shared geometry, material accounting and observation support; no apparatus or material is supplied by implementation. Study takes three rounds for suitability assessment, safe separation and conservation handling; development and review advance no simulation time.
